reasons.A: Period diction and measured sentences fit, but the rhythm is flatter and more narrative, lacking the author's compact ironic generalisations and wry turns.
reasons.B: Modern register and movement (present tense, 'Take a...', 'keeping score', clipped fragments-in-series) read as a contemporary essayist, not the genteel ironic voice of the passage.
reasons.C: Closest in movement and stance: short declaratives mixed with balanced aphoristic sentences ('seldom candid, for it is seldom disinterested'), genteel period diction, and a dry ironic close with an inclusive 'we' like the passage's 'delights us'.
